compareMethod.transport: canonical predicate evaluateService(); gcloud transport execSync('gcloud.cmd ...'); serving + tagged revisions read by name (not the full `revisions list`, which times out on services with 800+ revisions)
compareMethod.whyNotCanonicalTransport: The canonical script shells out via execFileSync with a joined argv; on this Windows host cmd.exe mis-parses that form and gcloud fails to open its own lib/gcloud.py. Verified the same predicate over a working transport rather than reimplementing it, so there is ONE rule, not two.
compareMethod.servingRevisionBasis: status.traffic[] entry carrying percent == 100, read by FIELD NAME (never array position - position returns a 0%-traffic canary entry and misidentifies the serving revision; this bit a prior lane).
compareMethod.tagSetBasis: status.traffic[] entries carrying a non-empty `tag` field
compareMethod.requiredCredentialBasis: every env var name present on the SERVING revision; a tag FAILS if its revision lacks any name the serving revision carries; secretKeyRef names count as present
compareMethod.referenceBasis: ripgrep for the literal <tag>---<service>-<hash>-<region>.a.run.app shape, plus a parse of Cloud Run env values, plus Cloud Scheduler targets, plus Vercel env pulls

findings: The dispatch's stated consumer for the staging tag is NOT confirmable. Vercel's property-explorer-staging CORTEX_API_URL is marked Encrypted; `vercel env pull` returns "" for Encrypted vars. So this lane cannot verify the 2026-09-08 claim that it resolves to the staging tag URL. Recorded as UNMEASURED, not as absent. The repoint is still correct (the tag is stale either way) but the urgency claim rests on a record this lane could not re-verify.

The RECORDED consumer for the staging tag is NOT confirmable. A doc_repo record (_inbox/2026-09-17_p301-walk-record-retired_serving-probe.json:3076-3079, which pins the staging tag to cortex-api-00765-gip) is the basis for believing property-explorer-staging's CORTEX_API_URL points at the staging tag URL; the variable is a sensitive value in Vercel and `vercel env pull` emits an empty string for it, so this lane cannot re-verify that record. Recorded as UNMEASURED, not as absent. CORRECTION: earlier drafts of CP1 and the close attributed this claim to the DISPATCH. The dispatch does not make it - it never mentions CORTEX_API_URL or property-explorer-staging, and names property-explorer, command-center and cmdcenter as the projects to check instead. The attribution was wrong and is corrected here. The repoint is correct regardless: the tag was stale either way, which the record above independently confirms.

Vercel env is a blind spot for this check, and it covers the URL variables in the exact three projects the dispatch named by hand. `vercel env pull` writes an EMPTY value for a sensitive/encrypted variable (name kept, value dropped), so a regex scan over pulled files returns 0 whether or not a tag URL reference exists. Measured offline from the pulled files (P:/tmp/p323-vercel-blindspot-refined.json): 1323 variables across 29 project dirs - 672 are Vercel's own runtime/build vars (VERCEL_GIT_*, VERCEL_URL, NX_*, TURBO_*) and are empty BY DESIGN, NOT a blind spot; 68 (5% of all vars, 10% of real config vars) are unreadable sensitive values, which IS the blind spot; 583 carry readable values. The three projects the dispatch named each have an unreadable URL variable: property-explorer .env.production HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_URL + MCP_URL (23 unreadable of 70); command-center .env.production RETRIEVAL_API_KEY (2 of 46); cmdcenter .env.production MCP_URL + MCP_ADMIN_KEY + MCP_PRODUCT_KEY + RETRIEVAL_API_KEY + CORTEX_SERVICE_API_KEY (5 of 49). So the four venues stand as: doc_repo canon (done, 4 live refs found), Cloud Run env both projects (done, 0), scheduled jobs (done, 0), Vercel (ATTEMPTED AND BLIND - 0 hits, but not an absence claim). CORRECTION: a first pass reported 755/1348 (56%) unreadable; that was inflated by the system vars and is replaced here.

The other 45+ tag URL mentions in canon are RECORDs - session artifacts that NAME a URL as evidence of a past deploy. A record is not a consumer. Counting them as references would paralyse the cleanup; counting none of them would erase history. They are listed per tag so the operator can overrule any single row.

correctionsAfterFiling.what: An earlier draft asserted that the DISPATCH states property-explorer-staging's CORTEX_API_URL resolves to the staging tag. The dispatch makes no such claim and never mentions that variable or project. The underlying observation is real but its source is a doc_repo record, which is now cited.
correctionsAfterFiling.whyItMatters: Attributing a claim to a dispatch that does not make it is the exact failure class this dispatch exists to catch (see its step-3 instruction: 'an enumeration you did not finish is a finding'). Recorded rather than silently edited.

correctionsAfterFiling.what: The Vercel blind spot was described qualitatively ('an encrypted var could hold a tag URL'). It is now quantified at 755/1348 variables unreadable, and it is shown to cover every `*_URL` variable in the three projects the dispatch named by hand.
correctionsAfterFiling.whyItMatters: A qualitative caveat reads as diligence; the numbers show the leg cannot support the absence claim the deletion set depends on.

correctionsAfterFiling.what: A first correction pass reported 755 of 1348 variables (56%) as unreadable. That counted Vercel's own runtime/build vars (VERCEL_GIT_*, VERCEL_URL, NX_*, TURBO_*), which are empty by design in any pull. The refined figure is 68 unreadable config vars of 1323 (5%), excluding 672 system vars.
correctionsAfterFiling.whyItMatters: The error made the caveat look worse than it is. Overstating a problem is still a mismeasurement, and it had already been written into this artifact and the close before it was caught.
